title: Web client: block/unblock button in contact list
description:
Since auto-discovery adds all tailnet kithd peers as contacts, users need a way to block contacts they do not want to chat with. Add a block/unblock toggle button to each contact row in renderContactList.

What: Modify renderContactList() in app.js to include a block/unblock button per contact item. Also add CSS.

Algorithm:
1. In renderContactList(contactList), for each contact <li>:
   a. Add a <button class='block-btn'> to each item, positioned to the right of the contact name.
   b. If contact.blocked is true: button text = 'Unblock', title = 'Unblock this contact'.
   c. If contact.blocked is false: button text = 'Block', title = 'Block this contact'.
   d. Button click handler (stopPropagation to prevent triggering openOrCreateChat):
      - const newBlocked = !contact.blocked;
      - Disable the button immediately (prevent double-click).
      - await setContactBlocked(contact.id, newBlocked);
      - (renderContactList re-renders in setContactBlocked on success; button re-enabled by re-render)
      - On error: re-enable button.
   e. The contact list should show blocked contacts (greyed out) with their block button, so users can see and unblock them. Adjust renderContactList to NOT skip blocked contacts — show them with a .blocked class instead.
      EXCEPTION: do not open a chat when clicking a blocked contact (check contact.blocked in openOrCreateChat and skip if blocked).

2. In style.css:
   - .contact-item.blocked: greyed out opacity, italic name, subtle visual difference
   - .block-btn: small, right-aligned, low-contrast button; red tint when showing 'Block', neutral when showing 'Unblock'
   - .block-btn:hover: slightly more prominent

3. Update openOrCreateChat() to check if contact.blocked and show an error ('Contact is blocked — unblock to send messages') instead of creating the chat.

Tests (independent oracle: DOM structure inspection):
- Test: renderContactList with one unblocked contact; assert DOM has a button with text 'Block'.
- Test: renderContactList with one blocked contact; assert li has class 'blocked' and button text 'Unblock'.
- Test: clicking Block button calls setContactBlocked(id, true).
- Test: clicking contact name when contact.blocked=true does NOT call openOrCreateChat.

Defensive programming rules:
- Use textContent for all button labels and contact names (never innerHTML)
- stopPropagation on button click to prevent chat open
- Disable button during async setContactBlocked call (prevent double-click)
- contact.id comes from the contacts Map (module state), not reconstructed from DOM
